Respondent :- State of U.P. and Another 
Counsel for Appellant :- Brajesh Kumar Solanki,Ajeet Kumar,Mahendra Kumar Yadav

Counsel for Respondent :- G.A.,Jitendra Kumar Yadav 
Hon'ble Siddharth, J.
1. Heard learned counsel for the appellant; learned Aga for opposite party no.1; Jitendra Kumar
Yadav, learned counsel for opposite party no.2 and perused the material placed on record.
2.

The present criminal appeal under Section 14-A(2) Scheduled Castes & Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act has been filed by the appellant to set aside the impugned order dated 18.10.2022, whereby the Special Judge, SC/ST Act, Pilibhit has rejected the bail application of the appellant moved by him in Case Crime No. 711 of 2022, under Sections- 376, 506 IPC and Section 67-A Information of Technology Act and 3(2)(V) SC/ST Act, Police Station- Pooranpur, District- Pilibhit.

entities.text: Scheduled Castes & Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 3. There is allegation in the FIR that on 02.01.2022 at about 08:00 a.m the prosecuterix was taking bath on the handpump inside her house when the appellant made her video and took other pictures in nude position.
By extending threats of making the video viral, he repeatedly committed the offence of rape against the victim.
When she informed her husband and he tried to talk with the appellant he ran away from his house to different kasba.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant submits that it is a case of false implication of the appellant.
In the medical examination report, no injury was found on her body.
The allegation of making any incriminating video viral is incorrect.
Monu Kumar, on whose phone the incriminating video was transferred was unable to produce the same and had stated that he has deleted the same.
The appellant is in jail since 08.09.2022 and has no criminal history to his credit.
It is a case of malicious prosecution under the provisions of SC/ST Act.

5. Learned A.G.A and learned counsel for the informant-opposite party no. 2 have vehemently opposed the bail application and have submitted that the argument made by the learned counsel for the appellant is incorrect.
The appellant had forwarded the screenshot of the photograph of the victim on the mobile phone of Saurabh Pratap Singh, which was produced by him before the investigating officer.
Certificate under Section 65-B of the Evidence Act was also obtained by the investigating officer.
Saurabh Pratap Singh, informed that the applicant had sent the photographs of the victim to many persons on their mobile phones.
6. After hearing the rival contentions, this Court finds that it is not a fit case for granting bail to the appellant at this stage.
7. The criminal appeal is accordingly, dismissed.
8. Trial court is directed to conclude the trial of the appellant as expeditiously as possible preferably within a period of one year from the date of production of certified copy of this order.
